## Research

My research is on what happens to people in the years after a myocardial infarction — how much life expectancy is lost, how that can be estimated well enough to be useful in the clinic, and what secondary prevention actually achieves. The work is mostly done in the national quality registries, above all SWEDEHEART, and in population cohorts such as SCAPIS.

Methodologically I work with time-to-event analysis — competing risks, relative survival and loss of life expectancy — along with propensity-score methods, Bayesian survival models and machine-learning approaches to risk prediction. I write the analyses myself, in R and Quarto, under version control.

I co-supervise a doctoral project at Karolinska Institutet on heart failure after myocardial infarction.

I have received research funding from the Swedish Heart-Lung Foundation, ALF Region Stockholm, Region Skåne and the Department of Cardiology at Danderyd University Hospital, and from an industry collaboration with Merck.

```{r}
## Publications - change google id here
pubs <- scholar::get_publications("S3TOd7gAAAAJ") %>% tibble() %>%
  mutate(url = scholar::get_article_scholar_url("S3TOd7gAAAAJ", pubid = pubid)) %>%
  arrange(desc(year))

# manual removal of some entries
remove_ <- c("Early Subjective Improvement of Exercise Capacity is an Indpendent Predictor of Long Term Survival in Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy Patients",
             "Long-term results of cardiac resynchronization therapy: A comparison between CRT-pacemakers versus primary prophylactic CRT-defibrillators (vol 38, pg 758, 2015)",
             "3291 Achieved biventricular pacing during the first year of follow-up predicts long-term outcome in patients with heart failure treated with cardiac resynchronization therapy",
             "P1950 CHA2DS2-VASC score in a cohort of CRT patients",
             "CHA2DS2-VASC score in a cohort of CRT patients",
             "Ventricular high rate episodes predict increased mortality in heart failure patients treated with CRT (vol 49, pg 20, 2015)",
             "P5683 Incremental hazard associated with the degree of advanced intaratrial block in cardiac resynchronization therapy treated heart failure patients",
             "Reclassification of Treatment Strategy With Instantaneous Wave-Free Ratio and Fractional Flow Reserve",
             "Positive Response to Cardiac Resynchronization Therapy-The Role of NTproBNP",
             "Incremental hazard associated with the degree of advanced intaratrial block in cardiac resynchronization therapy treated heart failure patients",
             "Left ventricular systolic dysfunction after acute myocardial infarction is associated with a high symptom burden and worse secondary prevention",
             "Comparison of sodium-glucose co-transporter-2 inhibitors and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists in myocardial infarction patients with type 2 diabetes"
)
remove_id_ <- c("QIV2ME_5wuYC")

# ESC congress abstracts appear in European Heart Journal supplements with an
# article id like "ehae666". They are dropped by rule rather than by title, so
# that next year's crop does not creep back in. Nine were present in November
# 2026; the title list above catches three of them, this catches all.
pubs <- pubs %>%
  filter(!title %in% remove_,
         !pubid %in% remove_id_,
         !grepl("Supplement[_ ]?[0-9]", number))

# Google Scholar mangles some records: author degrees glued to surnames, and
# article ids split across `journal` and `number`. Corrected by hand, keyed on
# pubid so a changed title does not lose the fix.
fix_ <- tibble::tribble(
  ~pubid,          ~field,     ~value,
  "isC4tDSrTZIC",  "author",   "Malmqvist J, Wang C, Bergström G, Engström G, Hagström E, Juszczyk J, Kader R, Söderberg S, Östgren CJ, Reitan C, Jernberg T",
  "r0BpntZqJG4C",  "journal",  "European Heart Journal – Cardiovascular Pharmacotherapy",
  "r0BpntZqJG4C",  "number",   "pvag032",
  "TFP_iSt0sucC",  "journal",  "European Heart Journal – Cardiovascular Pharmacotherapy",
  "TFP_iSt0sucC",  "number",   "pvag059",
  "j3f4tGmQtD8C",  "journal",  "European Heart Journal – Quality of Care and Clinical Outcomes",
  "j3f4tGmQtD8C",  "number",   "qcag071"
)
for (i in seq_len(nrow(fix_)))
  pubs[pubs$pubid == fix_$pubid[i], fix_$field[i]] <- fix_$value[i]

# add information to thesis
pubs <- pubs %>%
  mutate(journal = ifelse(pubid == "WF5omc3nYNoC", 'Lund University, Thesis', journal))


# format for markdown
pubs <- pubs %>%
  mutate(title = sub("\\.$", "", title),
         out = paste0("[", author, " (", year, "). ", title, ". *", journal, "*. ", number,"](", url, ")\n\n")) %>%
  select(title, out)

cat(pubs$out)
```
